20260815-festival-of-new-texas-plays-by-.title: Festival of New Texas Plays by Austin Playhouse
20260815-festival-of-new-texas-plays-by-.rss_description_html:
2026 Festival of New Texas Plays

 

ACES by Emilie Budjaja

Saturday, August 15, 2026 at 4 pm

Questions of language, identity, and belonging combine into an experience that is funny, moving and magical. The play interweaves two storylines twenty years apart, revealing how the same hopes, pressures, and sacrifices echo across generations. Partially performed in Mandarin with no subtitles, it asks the audience to experience, rather than just observe, the struggle to understand one anothe

 

Lulu Goes to the Jim Henson Memorial Service by Kleo James Ryan

Saturday, August 15, 2026 at 7:30 pm

A wonderfully theatrical blend of heart, humor, grief, and puppetry. Yes, puppetry. The conceit that nearly everyone except Lulu’s parents is a puppet allows the audience to see the world through Lulu’s imaginative and deeply felt (pun fully intended) perspective. It is genuinely hilarious, delightfully weird, and ultimately profoundly tender.

 

Mom and Pop by Carl Gonzales

Sunday, August 16, 2026 at 2 pm

A vivid exploration of family, culture, and community, set in a down-home restaurant where everyone dreams of bigger things. It is both a family comedy and a love letter to the Latine community - messy, exuberant, politically alive, and full of heart.

Feature by Brianna Culeri, www.culturemap. com, July 21, 2026

As part of Austin Playhouse’s dedication to supporting the new works of playwrights through world premieres, commissioned works, and new play festivals, the Festival of New Texas Plays celebrates works-in-progress from Texas-based playwrights.

Playwrights will be attendance at each performance with a talkback following each reading. There will be an opening mixer between performances on August 15 with light refreshments. Guests are welcome to stay after the 4 pm performance, arrive early for the 7:30 pm, or attend both. Sunday’s reading will conclude with a closing reception.

Finalist runners-up were Everyone, give yourselves a pat on the back! by Erin Malone Turner and I’M GONNA BE THE GOVERNOR by Ainsley Powers.

Semi-Finalists for the 2026 Festival of New Texas Plays are Peanut Is A Vibe by Nate Southard; Two Million Years of Rain by Sheree L. Ross; First by Joey Banks and Vee Council; T-minus-15 by Diamante Martinez; and The Lily Problem by Max Langert.

The selection committee for this year’s festival were Lowell Bartholomee, Brian Coughlin, Lara Toner Haddock, Tonie Knight, Stephen Mercantel, Laura Walberg, Cyndi Williams, and Ben Wolfe. 

About the Playwrights:

Emilie Budjaja (Playwright, ACES) is an Asian American screenwriter and playwright interested in writing stories that explore identity as a malleable form. A native from Austin, Texas, she recently earned her B.S. in Radio-Television-Film from UT Austin. During her time as a student, she acted as showrunner for the Texas Student Television’s half-hour comedy, The Austen Exchange, and has also served as a writer on the station’s first Mandarin speaking serialized drama. She is constantly working towards being in a room with other Asian American creatives, collaborating to make rich, embodied stories.

Carl Gonzales (Playwright, Mom and Pop) is a Mexican/Indigenous director, playwright, and actor. Recent directing credits include Pueblo Revolt (Ground Floor Theatre) Dulce (ASRT), Clyde’s (B. Iden Payne Award winner, Ground Floor Theatre), Anna in the Tropics (B. Iden Payne Award winner, Ground Floor Theatre), Tick, Tick... Boom! (TexArts), and The Brunch Crowd (Texas State University). Most recently, Carl’s play La Planchada was selected for the Teatrx Short Play Festival. Carl is also proud to serve as the Board Chair of Ground Floor Theatre and President of the B. Iden Payne Awards Council.

Kleo James Ryan (Playwright, Lulu Goes to the Jim Henson Memorial Service) is a writer/performer based in Austin, TX. Her short works include I’ll Make an End (FronteraFest 2024), The Woman in the Attic (FronteraFest 2025), Last Dance (Out of Ink 2025: In Step), Famous Last Words (Manifest Minifest 6), and Wollstonecraft/Shelley (Out of Ink 2026: Astronomical). Her full-length play, The Hooded Crow, was a recipient of ScriptWorks’s Revision Resource Fund, and received a public developmental reading at Ground Floor Theatre in 2025. Kleo’s plays were awarded “Best of Week” at FronteraFest two years in a row. Her short play, Last Dance, was nominated for five B. Iden Payne Awards, including Outstanding Original Short Script and Outstanding Production of a Short Play. Kleo is currently developing a stage adaptation of Emily Brontë’s Wuthering Heights.

Sponsors: Austin Playhouse is supported in part by Texas Commission on the Arts, The Shubert Foundation, and an Elevate Grant of Austin Arts, Culture, Music, and Entertainment.

Austin Playhouse is a professional theatre in its 26th season. Currently under the leadership of Producing Artistic Director Lara Toner Haddock, and Associate Artistic Directors Ben Wolfe and Sarah Fleming Walker, Austin Playhouse has grown from a three-play season on the campus of Concordia University, to a year-round operation producing a subscription season, theatre for youth productions, and a new play festival. Austin Playhouse plans to build a permanent home for the veteran theatre troupe and all of Austin’s artistic community. For more information visit austinplayhouse.com.

20270612-silent-sky-by-camille-lightner-.title: Silent Sky by Camille Lightner Playhouse
20270612-silent-sky-by-camille-lightner-.rss_description_html:
Silent Sky tells the true story of Henrietta Leavitt, the astronomer ahead of her time. It is 1900, and Henrietta has the opportunity to work at Harvard University as a human computer, one of Dr. Edward Pickering’s “harem,” mapping the stars but receiving no scientific credit. When Henrietta arrives, she is eager to use Harvard’s telescope - the Great Refractor - but is told that she will not be able to do any sort of astronomical discovery as she will only log the stars photographed by the men of the department.

However, Henrietta will not be dissuaded, and begins the process of recording the changes in Cepheid stars - a scientific discovery that has profound and lasting impact on the field of astronomy. During her inquiry, Henrietta’s relationships strain under her obsessive work ethic; her sister Margaret, her love interest Peter Shaw, and her colleagues Annie Cannon and Williamina Fleming all find themselves pushed aside in favor of a great cosmic mystery.

Silent Sky is the poignant tale of a woman’s dedication to the stars, and the human touch that makes life under the vast sky beautiful and timeless.

This show will be performed in the round, in our DeStefano Room. Tickets will be limited!

20270514-the-play-that-goes-wrong-by-cam.title: The Play That Goes Wrong by Camille Lightner Playhouse
20270514-the-play-that-goes-wrong-by-cam.rss_description_html:
The Play That Goes Wrong begins before the curtain has even been raised, as the audience are present while the Cornley Polytechnic Drama Society prepare to stage their new production the 1920s murder mystery Murder at Haversham Manor.' However, the set is not yet complete and there is no time to finish it off…..the show must go on!

With a murder (and a moving corpse) established from the beginning, the murder mystery gets into full flow. However, the props start to disappear, actors go missing and the set begins to collapse around, and often on, the cast. Mayhem ensues, the acting gets worse, and the set becomes increasingly dangerous, but the company struggle on regardless. The question is whether any of the cast and crew will remain standing, or conscious, by the final curtain?!

20270402-nine-musical-by-camille-lightne.title: Nine, musical by Camille Lightner Playhouse
20270402-nine-musical-by-camille-lightne.rss_description_html: Nine centers around Guido Contini, a famous Italian film director and ladies man. His last couple of movies have been panned by the critics, and Guido is under pressure to make a return to form with his latest film. However, there is one major problem: he hasn’t written a line of the script and has lost all inspiration. Guido’s professional and personal lives becomes intertwined as he attempts to save both his career and his marriage. His wife, Luisa, threatens to divorce Guido unless he can pay more attention to the marriage, but the director is constantly pulled in another direction by his saucy mistress, Carla, who shows up at the most inconvenient times.

20270212-camelot-by-camille-lightner-pla.title: Camelot by Camille Lightner Playhouse
20270212-camelot-by-camille-lightner-pla.rss_description_html:
Lerner and Loewe’s majestic Camelot brings the legend of King Arthur and his Knights of the Round Table to life with an extraordinary score and a story that poignantly dramatizes the human conflict at the heart of this classic tale. Based on T.H. White’s novel The Once and Future King, Camelot tells the story of Arthur, a young squire who becomes King after extracting the sword Excalibur from its legendary rock.

Camelot opens in the midst of the battle that destroyed King Arthur’s kingdom and goes back to tell the story of how the battle came to be. The musical follows Arthur from a young, ambitious, idealistic King who dreams of creating a just society to the despairing king bearing witness to his dream’s demise. Arthur’s dream is inspired by his vivacious Queen Guenevere. Together, they create a kingdom where might works at the service of right and the King serves at a round table with no head — a symbol of collaboration and unity.

But just as this utopian vision starts to become reality, everything begins to unravel. When Guenevere falls in love with Arthur’s most celebrated, beloved, and loyal knight, Lancelot, they begin a romance as doomed as it is passionate. Their troubles are compounded when Arthur’s illegitimate son, Mordred, arrives on the scene. In a world of human realities, can Camelot achieve the utopia of which Arthur dreams?

20261211-cinderella-the-musical-by-rodge.title: Cinderella, the musical by Rodgers and Hammerstein by Camille Lightner Playhouse
20261211-cinderella-the-musical-by-rodge.rss_description_html:
Rodgers and Hammerstein’s enchanting adaptation of the timeless fairytale Cinderella was their only musical originally composed for television. When the television program, starring Julie Andrews as Cinderella, first aired in 1957, it was the most widely viewed program in the history of the medium at that time.

Since then, Rodgers and Hammerstein’s Cinderella has continued to charm audiences in productions on stage and on television. Based upon the classic fairy tale, and particularly the French version Cendrillon ou la Petite Pantoufle de Verre, Rodgers and Hammerstein’s adaptation brings new life to the story of a young woman forced into servitude who dreams of – and achieves – a better life. Cinderella features some of Rodgers and Hammerstein’s most beloved songs, including “In My Own Little Corner,” “Impossible,” and “Ten Minutes Ago.”

20261016-rumors-by-camille-lightner-play.title: Rumors by Camille Lightner Playhouse
20261016-rumors-by-camille-lightner-play.rss_description_html:
Chris and Ken Gorman arrive at a fancy dinner party for their friend, Charley Brock. They discover that all is not well, and that Charley has had an accident involving a shotgun and his earlobe. This could be damaging to Charley’s reputation, as he is deputy mayor of New York City. Chris and Ken’s friends begin to arrive. As they attempt to cover up the facts, hilarity ensues.

Neil Simon’s Rumors is a charming farce with lots of gags, twists, zingers, and zanies, but it also borrows from Simon’s life experience to depict the challenges, as well as the comforts, of married life.

20260911-rent-by-camille-lightner-playho.title: Rent by Camille Lightner Playhouse
20260911-rent-by-camille-lightner-playho.html_synopsis: Rent is a rock musical with music and lyrics by Jonathan Larson[1] loosely based on Giacomo Puccini's opera La bohème. It tells the story of a group of impoverished young artists struggling to survive and create a life in New York City's East Village in the thriving days of Bohemian Alphabet City, under the shadow of HIV/AIDS.

20260903-and-she-was-loved-by-black-rose.title: And She Was Loved by Black Rose Theatre
20260903-and-she-was-loved-by-black-rose.rss_description_html:
Black Rose Theatre presents a world premiere one-act play by Zell Miller III, And She Was Loved: A Ritual of Healing. A Celebration of Love. A Story of What Remains. 

Inspired by the loss of Miller’s mother, Vernell Miller, and his longtime mentor, theater icon Laurie Carlos, And She Was Loved is a deeply personal journey through grief, and memory that ultimately transforms into a testament of resilience, healing, and the enduring power of love.

Blending the mythology of Peter Pan with hip-hop theater, jazz aesthetics, movement, and gesture language, this powerful new work explores the bitter, the sweet, the love that remains after loss—and the hope that never leaves us.

Featuring national & international award-winning tap dancer Siobhan Alexis and introducing Marley Miller, granddaughter of Vernell Miller, and featuring Zell Miller III, Austin’s first poet laureate.

20270416-falstaff-by-butler-school-of-mu.title: Falstaff by Butler School of Music
20270416-falstaff-by-butler-school-of-mu.venue_address: Robert Dedman Drive and E. 23rd Street Campus of the University of Texas Austin, TX, 78712
20270416-falstaff-by-butler-school-of-mu.rss_description_html:
Falstaff  is a comic opera in three acts by the Italian composer Giuseppe Verdi. The Italian-language libretto was adapted by Arrigo Boito from the play The Merry Wives of Windsor and scenes from Henry IV, Part 1 and Part 2, by William Shakespeare. The work premiered on 9 February 1893 at La Scala, Milan.

Verdi wrote Falstaff, the last of his 26 operas, as he approached the age of 80. It was his second comedy, and his third work based on a Shakespeare play, following Macbeth and Otello. The plot revolves around the thwarted, sometimes farcical, efforts of the fat knight Sir John Falstaff to seduce two married women to gain access to their husbands' wealth.

Douglas Kinney Frost, conductor

Madison Jackson, stage director

 

Sung in Italian with supertitles.

20270218-ainadamar-by-butler-school-of-m.venue_address: Robert Dedman Drive and E. 23rd Street Campus of the University of Texas Austin, TX, 78712
20270218-ainadamar-by-butler-school-of-m.rss_description_html:
Described as “an opera in three images,” Ainadamar traces the life of Spanish poet and playwright Federico García Lorca as recounted by his muse and longtime collaborator, actress Margarita Xirgu. Over the course of the opera, Margarita relates episodes from Lorca’s life—his persecution for his political sympathies and his homosexuality, her attempts to persuade him to flee the Spanish Civil War, his death at the hands of the fascist Falangists—and the opera’s tone and structure reflect much of his writing, combining crude realism with transcendent idealism and imbuing the everyday with a sense of mythic ritual.

Sung in Italian with Spanish with supertitles.

20261016-i-capuleti-e-i-montecchi-by-but.title: I Capuleti e i Montecchi by Butler School of Music
20261016-i-capuleti-e-i-montecchi-by-but.venue_address: Robert Dedman Drive and E. 23rd Street Campus of the University of Texas Austin, TX, 78712
20261016-i-capuleti-e-i-montecchi-by-but.rss_description_html:
Douglas Kinney Frost, conductor

Yingmeige Xiong, stage director

Sung in Italian with English with supertitles.

I Capuleti e i Montecchi (The Capulets and the Montagues) is an Italian opera (tragedia lirica) in two acts by Vincenzo Bellini. The libretto by Felice Romani was a reworking of the story of Romeo and Juliet for an opera by Nicola Vaccai called Giulietta e Romeo and based on the play of the same name by Luigi Scevola written in 1818, thus an Italian source rather than taken directly from Shakespeare's play.

Bellini was persuaded to write the opera for the 1830 Carnival season at the Teatro La Fenice in Venice, with only a month and a half available for composition. He succeeded by appropriating a large amount of music previously written for his unsuccessful opera Zaira.

The first performance of I Capuleti e i Montecchi took place on 11 March 1830

20260919-through-crimson-eyes-by-coll-st.title: Through Crimson Eyes by Coll Street Players
20260919-through-crimson-eyes-by-coll-st.venue_address: First Protestant Church 172 W. Coll Street New Braunfels, TX, 78130
20260919-through-crimson-eyes-by-coll-st.rss_description_html:
As bombs rain over France during World War II, two children, Louis Hoffsteder and Carolyn Redgrave, discover a hidden doorway inside a hollow tree that leads to Wonderland—a mysterious world of breathtaking beauty and dangerous secrets. What begins as an escape from the horrors of war becomes their home – but Wonderland changes those who remain within it, feeding their deepest desires and slowly pulling them apart. As their love fractures and darkness spreads through Wonderland, the two are transformed into the very people they were never meant to become: Louis into the Mad Hatter and Carolyn into the ruthless Queen of Hearts—former lovers turned bitter enemies in a world that created them both.

Directed by Andrea Saur

We’re thrilled to welcome local playwrights Brook Feldman and Andrew Saur to the Coll Street Players stage for Through Crimson Eyes!
Join us for a play reading workshop and staged reading as we help shape this powerful new work on its journey to future seasons.
Emerging Works Table Read
 
Come be part of the creative process and see a new play take its first steps toward the spotlight
 
Ages 13-Adult
 
Check out more info on our website at https://collstreetplayers.com/through-crimson-eyes/

Waking from hibernation in the Spring, Frog and Toad plant gardens, swim, rake leaves, go sledding and learn life lessons along the way. Book and Lyrics by Willie Reale
Music by Robert Reale

20270220-awesome-allie-first-kid-astrona.title: Awesome Allie: First Kid Astronaut by Scottish Rite Theater
20270220-awesome-allie-first-kid-astrona.html_synopsis: Yesterday Allie was just a normal kid, but today she’s headed into outer space! With the help of her trusty talking dog Captain Chaos and Rover the Dancing Robot from Mars, Allie’s on a mission across the solar system to save Earth, and maybe learn some things about science along the way. 20261204-a-christmas-carol-catastrophe-b.title: A Christmas Carol Catastrophe by Crown Theatre
20261204-a-christmas-carol-catastrophe-b.rss_description_html:
Christmas comes once a year, and is a time that opens the door to memories of holidays past, gratitude for blessings present, and hopes for a prosperous future. So, what better way to celebrate this special time, than to put on a show?! And not just ANY show, but THE show. 
 
Join a ragtag troupe of performers as the desperately try to put on the most profound and moving production ever produced of Charles Dickens’ “A Christmas Carol”…..within budget. 
 
Unfortunately, things don’t work out as planned. The venue has been double booked, the beleaguered stage manager is performing double duty as Bob Cratchit, and the actor playing Ebeneezer Scrooge is missing, forcing the even-more beleaguered director, to play the role. 
 
This band of merrymakers attempts to bring it all together despite facing hurdle after hurdle that threatens to ruin the holiday spirit and stop the show for good. But, ever the consummate professionals, the show must go on, and the gang do their best to arrive at “God bless us, everyone”, as they discover along the way that love, hope, and friendship are some of the most beautiful blessings we hold, no matter the time of year.
 
Written by Trey Deason
Directed by Tobie Minor

20260814-the-musical-comedy-murders-of-1.title: The Musical Comedy Murders of 1940 by Chambers Theatre Company
20260814-the-musical-comedy-murders-of-1.venue_address: 121 N. Main Street Inspired Minds Arts Center Buda, TX, 78710
20260814-the-musical-comedy-murders-of-1.rss_description_html:
An eccentric theatre financier has gathered a team at her mansion in New York. Everyone believes that they will have a backer’s audition to get an investment for their newest musical. However, the shadow of the team’s last show hangs over the group—due mysterious murders committed by the “Stage Door Slasher.” An undercover police officer is hoping to flush out the killer from this group of suspects. Throw in blizzard conditions and secret passageways to create an Agatha-Christie-meets-Clue formula of whodunnit parody. The Musical Comedy Murders of 1940 is full of delightful slapstick for audience of all ages.

A whodunit plot set during a rehearsal for a new musical
 
The Musical Comedy Murders of 1940 is a comedic murder mystery play by John Bishop, known for its witty dialogue, farcical situations, and a whodunit plot set during a rehearsal for a new musical. The play follows a group of characters, including a detective and a composer, as they try to solve the murder of a producer, all while dealing with the chaos of a show in development, leading to a series of hilarious and unexpected twists.
 
Directed by Ameer Mobarak

20260911-primary-trust-by-austin-playhou.title: Primary Trust by Austin Playhouse
20260911-primary-trust-by-austin-playhou.rss_description_html:
Welcome friend, you are right on time! 

Kenneth has everything he needs: a job he loves, his best friend Bert, and daily mai tais at Wally’s. It’s a comforting, secure routine — until he finds himself unemployed. With Bert’s encouragement, Kenneth applies to be a teller at Primary Trust Bank. Thriving at work, he slowly begins to open his heart to new people and possibilities. But when newfound rhythms threaten his friendship with Bert, Kenneth must face his past before he can fully embrace his future.Currently one of the most produced plays in the country right now, Primary Trust is an intimate and heartwarming story of friendship, resilience, and the search for human connection that shines a spotlight on the small moments that make life worthwhile.

Ben Wolfe directs. “On my first reading of Primary Trust, I felt a deep kinship with Kenneth—living a structured life, comfortable in his routines, and struggling to connect with others when those routines are suddenly changed. I was immediately struck by the depth of its simplicity: exploring the human experience, finding meaning in the ebb and flow of ordinary life, and inviting us to see how small acts of kindness, patience, and community can transform a life,” said Wolfe. “I think now is the right time to tell this story because it offers the perfect antidote when we're feeling overwhelmed—by the world, the news, or life itself. It’s exactly the kind of story that I love to tell at Austin Playhouse: intimate, deeply human, and full of hope.”

 

 

Directed by Associate Artistic Director Ben Wolfe. The additional creative team includes Glenda Wolfe as costume designer: Mark Novick as lighting designer; Mike Toner as scenic designer; Robert S. Fisher as sound designer; Barry Miller as stage manager; and Kollin Clarke as assistant stage manager.

Content Advisory: Recommended for ages 13 and up. Children under 5 are not permitted.

20270320-pinocchio-davies-by-opera-san-a.title: Pinocchio (Davies) by Opera San Antonio
20270320-pinocchio-davies-by-opera-san-a.venue_address: 420 South Alamo Street San Antonio, TX, 78205
20270320-pinocchio-davies-by-opera-san-a.rss_description_html:
One of the most beloved characters in children’s literature takes center stage in this magical re-telling, which blends opera and theatrical staging. Pinocchio captures the childlike curiosity in all of us as he navigates an unknown and complicated world. When persuaded by the mischievous duo, Wolf and Cat, Pinocchio disobeys his father, Gepetto, and skips school. Of course, his journey is met by the notorious Dr. Dulcamara, a loathsome puppeteer, and his mechanical doll Olympia. Through a series of adventures, Pinocchio learns the harsh reality that every untruth comes with real-world consequences, the importance of sharing the truth with trusted grownups, and ultimately, the meaning of family. Your favorite wooden marionette comes alive for 3-weekends only in this age-old story of truthfulness, bravery, and heart! San Antonio’s not-to-miss artistic collaboration of 2027.

By John Davies
Based on The Adventures of Pinocchio by Carlo Collodi with scenes from operas by Mozart, Donizetti, Offenbach, and Pergolesi

Magik Theatre & OPERA San Antonio present John Davies’ Pinocchio, a one-act opera for young audiences based on Carlo Collodi’s literary classic, featuring music from operas by Mozart, Donizetti, Offenbach, and Pergolesi.


Recommended for ages 4+
Running Time: 55 minutes
Language: English

20260808-if-i-could-turn-back-time-by-gu.title: If I Could Turn Back Time by Guadalupe Cultural Arts Center
20260808-if-i-could-turn-back-time-by-gu.rss_description_html:
After the sudden death of their sister, Julio returns to their family home in the South Texas borderlands for the funeral. Once there, Julio must navigate grief while confronting an estranged family that disapproves of their involvement in the drag community. Encouraged by their late sister's spirit, Julio summons strength by stepping into their drag persona, Sharona, for the remainder of the visit. As Sharona, she builds unexpected connections, heals old wounds, and finds a way to let go of past pain while accepting her sister’s passing.
 
The Guadalupe Cultural Arts Center’s Theater Arts program is proud to present the 2026 Teatro Salón Table Readers Series, If I Could Turn Back Time by Gerry Rodriguez. This reading is directed by Marisela Barrera.
 
Hosted at the Guadalupe Latino Bookstore,1300 Guadalupe St., this dynamic series invites the public to experience the exciting early stages of script development in an intimate setting. Admission is free.
 
About the Playwright:
Gerry Rodriguez is a poet and playwright from Mission, TX, holding an MFA in Creative Writing from UTRGV. She teaches college-level English Composition and Rhetoric, serves as the founder and Artistic Director of the Rio Grande Valley Playwrights Circle, and is VP of Operations for Palabrandar Theatre Company.
 
About the Director:
Marisela Barrera (BFA, MA, MFA) is an award-winning Tejana teatrista—writer, actor, stage director, cultural activist, and border goth storyteller whose genre-bending work bridges the Tex-Mex frontera, the classroom, and radical Chicana/Latina arts spaces.
 
About Teatro Salon Reading Series:
Selected through an open call for new works, this year’s spotlighted plays showcase powerful Tejana and South Texas voices. Staged by local actors and directors, each reading offers audiences a unique glimpse into the creative process, followed by an interactive Question & Answer session with the playwrights, directors, and readers.

20260815-welcome-to-the-neighborhood-by-.title: Welcome to the Neighborhood by Guadalupe Cultural Arts Center
20260815-welcome-to-the-neighborhood-by-.rss_description_html:
Set in a suburban Texas community, Welcome to the Neighborhood explores the mounting tensions among neighbors as personal beliefs collide with contemporary social and political divisions. When a conflict escalates to a dangerous breaking point, the Virgen de Guadalupe appears in a miraculous moment. In the aftermath, as the community awaits her return, the neighbors begin to confront their differences and discover a shared capacity for forgiveness, understanding, and acceptance.
 
The Guadalupe Cultural Arts Center’s Theater Arts program is proud to present the 2026 Teatro Salón Table Readers Series, Welcome to the Neighborhood, by playwright Marissa Castañón-Hernández. This special reading takes place on Saturday, August 15 at 2:00 PM. This reading is directed by Clint Taylor.
 
Hosted at the Guadalupe Latino Bookstore,1300 Guadalupe St., this dynamic series invites the public to experience the exciting early stages of script development in an intimate setting. Admission is free.
 
About the Playwright: Marissa Castañón-Hernández is an Austin-based educator, writer, and award-winning playwright whose work—featured in the Austin American-Statesman and on stages from Repertorio Español to the Vortex Theatre—champions educational justice and amplifies the voices of historically marginalized communities.
 
About the Director: Clint George Taylor is the Guadalupe Cultural Arts Center’s Theater Arts Program Assistant and a multifaceted San Antonio-based artist, educator, and community leader, active with Jump-Start Performance Co. and co-creator of Better Butter the Show, using performance, writing, and production to champion arts education and marginalized voices.

20261001-the-color-purple-the-musical-by.title: The Color Purple, the musical by Temple Civic Theatre
20261001-the-color-purple-the-musical-by.rss_description_html:
Set in rural Georgia during the early 1900s, the story follows Celie, a young woman whose voice has been silenced by years of abuse and hardship. Through the unwavering support of extraordinary women and the transformative power of faith, friendship, and self-discovery, Celie finds the courage to reclaim her life,

POWERFUL. HEARTBREAKING. TRIUMPHANT.

Based on Alice Walker's Pulitzer Prize-winning novel and the acclaimed Broadway musical, The Color Purple is an unforgettable story of resilience, hope, and the healing power of love.

This is the one.

Not every show comes along with the power to change the people on stage and the people in the audience.
The Color Purple is one of those shows.

20270528-you-are-cordially-invited-to-th.title: You Are Cordially Invited to the End of the World by Austin Playhouse
20270528-you-are-cordially-invited-to-th.rss_description_html:
When Greg gets a terminal diagnosis, his small family feels the pressure of time running out. His wife Viv wants nothing more than to savor every last minute together. His child works to find meaning in the chaos. Meanwhile, Greg feels a new connection to the fate of our planet. Can saving the world save Greg?  Maybe? After all, the world’s too big not to be kind of magical. 

​ REGIONAL PREMIERE

Why we love it: This laugh-out-loud, wildly imaginative experience speaks to the very real issues of climate anxiety and grief without dwelling in hopelessness. It creates opportunities to talk about big, meaningful issues with compassion, humor, and unexpected joy.

20270326-into-the-woods-by-austin-playho.title: Into The Woods by Austin Playhouse
20270326-into-the-woods-by-austin-playho.rss_description_html:
In Sondheim’s dazzling musical, fairy tale characters such as Jack (of beanstalk fame), Little Red Riding Hood, Cinderella, and Rapunzel take us beyond happily ever after to discover what really matters in life. Beloved for nearly 40 years, and filled with soaring songs like “No One Is Alone” and “Children Will Listen,” Into the Woods is a joyful and moving exploration of how to be human. 

Why we love it: This musical with its incredible score and iconic characters is a perfect fit for Austin Playhouse. Our company will reimagine the ultimate storytelling musical for an intimate ensemble of 10 versatile performers. Audiences will feel closer than ever to these stories as the fairy tale world is created with true theatre magic, letting the play’s timeless message about the power of community to create their own happy ending take center stage.

20270129-the-revolutionists-by-austin-pl.title: The Revolutionists by Austin Playhouse
20270129-the-revolutionists-by-austin-pl.rss_description_html:
​​Four beautiful, badass women lose their heads in this irreverent comedy. Join playwright Olympe de Gouges, assassin Charlotte Corday, Haitian rebel Marianne Angelle, and former queen Marie Antoinette as they hang out, murder Marat and try to beat back the extremist insanity in 1793 Paris. This grand and dream-tweaked comedy is about violence and legacy, art and activism, feminism and terrorism, compatriots and chosen sisters and how we actually go about changing the world. 

 

Why we love it: Lauren Gunderson (Silent Sky, Christmas at Pemberley) is one of our favorite playwrights, and the most-produced playwright in America. The Revolutionists has her signature blend of fresh, thought-provoking ideas brought to life by wonderfully witty and bold characters.

20270418-la-traviata-by-austin-opera.title: La Traviata by Austin Opera
20270418-la-traviata-by-austin-opera.rss_description_html:
Violetta is the life of the party! As the most sought-after courtesan in Paris, she has it all: fame, fortune, and influence—but love will cost her everything. While entertaining Parisian socialites at one of her fashionable salons, she meets the young Alfredo, a man of good family and rigid social expectations. 

Alfredo’s sincere devotion offers her a glimpse of a new life, and their love blossoms, shadowed by her health and society’s unforgiving gaze. When Alfredo’s father, Giorgio Germont, confronts Violetta and demands she abandon his son to preserve family honor, their happiness is torn apart, and fate begins its cruel work.

From its aching, foreshadowing prelude to its popular, raucous choruses, Verdi’s La traviata features some of opera’s most recognizable ensembles and one of its ultimate soprano roles—showcasing why it remains one of the most famous and frequently performed operas in the world.

Featuring the Austin Opera Orchestra & Chorus conducted by Timothy Myers.

Sung in Italian with English projected titles
Performance run time: 2 hours and 40 minutes with 1 intermission

A co-production with Opera San Antonio made possible with support from The Dr. M. Lee Pearce Foundation.

Chicago Lyric Opera Production/Desmond Heeley

20270206-fellow-travelers-by-austin-oper.title: Fellow Travelers by Austin Opera
20270206-fellow-travelers-by-austin-oper.rss_description_html:
In 1953, the young, idealistic Timothy Laughlin arrives in Washington, D.C., eager to join the fight against Communism. A chance encounter with Hawkins Fuller, a State Department official, results in Tim’s first job and his first romantic relationship with a man. As Tim struggles to reconcile his newfound love with his beliefs, the baleful force of McCarthyism threatens to cost Hawkins his job and his freedom.

Called “a deeply human love story” by the Chicago Tribune, Fellow Travelers portrays the experiences of government employees who were subject to humiliating investigations because of their sexuality.

Austin Opera’s performances in February 2027 kick off the second year of a national tour that will bring this story to multiple cities across the US in 2026 and 2027, one of the largest consortium projects ever attempted in the US opera industry. The tour is being co-produced by the Up Until Now Collective. In 2026, the tour begins with Seattle Opera (February 21-March 1), Portland Opera (March 7–15), San Diego Opera (July 10–12) and New York’s Glimmerglass Festival (July 18–Aug. 16). 

“As we prepare to celebrate the opera’s tenth anniversary, I have been reflecting on my values as an artist, especially as a Queer artist making work during these uncertain times,” says stage director Kevin Newbury, who also directed the premiere of Fellow Travelers at Cincinnati Opera in 2016. “I believe that we stand on the shoulders of the people who came before us and who fought so hard and sacrificed so much for us to have the rights we have today. I believe in the power of art to build community. And I believe in the power of a good love story. And Fellow Travelers is, first and foremost, a good love story.”

20261113-thais-by-austin-opera.title: Thaïs by Austin Opera
20261113-thais-by-austin-opera.rss_description_html:
Famed enchantress Thaïs is the most admired woman in Alexandria, whose beauty and charisma have captivated the city. Entertaining the city’s elite with wit, artistry, and charm, she commands devotion wherever she appears.

Devoted to the goddess Venus, her life is one of excess, until a profound encounter alters her destiny. Athanaël, a monk devoted to God, cannot ignore the spell Thaïs casts over Alexandria, nor the worldly pleasures that define her life. Driven to save her from spiritual ruin, he pursues her relentlessly, and what begins as a mission of faith becomes a consuming obsession—one where the choices they make will decide who will triumph: faith or desire.

Synopsis available HERE

Sarah and Ernest Butler Music Director Timothy Myers conducts the Austin Opera Orchestra & Chorus in a profound new production and immersive opera experience!

Thaïs is part of Opera Unleashed. A series dedicated to bringing company premieres and epic masterpieces to Austin Opera audiences.

Sung in French with projected English titles
Performance run time: 2 hours and 45 minutes with 1 intermission
Thaïs is a co-Prodction between Spoleto Festival USA and Austin Opera.

20270408-la-traviata-by-opera-san-antoni.title: La Traviata by Opera San Antonio
20270408-la-traviata-by-opera-san-antoni.venue_name: Tobin Center for the Performing Arts
20270408-la-traviata-by-opera-san-antoni.rss_description_html:
A work of heartbreaking beauty and emotional power, La traviata follows Violetta’s journey through love, sacrifice, and societal judgment, all set to some of Verdi’s most beloved and soaring music. Desmond Heeley’s designs have been celebrated for their beauty and grandeur, making this a Traviata of rare visual richness and musical intensity. Audiences can expect exquisite costumes, stunning visuals, and world-class operatic voices in one of opera’s most timeless and devastating masterpieces.

OPERA San Antonio reunites with Austin Opera for La traviata, presented in the famed Desmond Heeley production originally created for Lyric Opera of Chicago.

Sung in Italian with English translations projected above the stage.

This production is presented in collaboration with The Orchestra San Antonio and Austin Opera.

free pre-show lectures:

One hour prior to each performance, audience members are encouraged to attend a free lecture that is open to all ticket holders. These lectures, held in the Tobin Center’s Feik Rotunda, are designed to be educational for opera-goers of all ages and are offered to help the audience gain a better understanding of the production they are about to experience.

Overview

Music by: Giuseppe Verdi
Libretto by: Francesco Maria Piave
Running Time: 3 hours including one intermission

Austin Opera

20260825-a-few-tiny-acres-by-cinnamon-pa.title: A Few Tiny Acres by Cinnamon Path Theater
20260825-a-few-tiny-acres-by-cinnamon-pa.rss_description_html:
Three executives, an international diplomat, and a mysterious squatter with a bulldozer collide over a single plot of land. What begins as a routine corporate acquisition quickly devolves into the grand opening of a "data center park" – a fragile, architectural nightmare where danger lurks behind every motherboard.
Tickets are free and are recommended to save a place.
 
A staged reading of A Few Tiny Acres by Max Langert
 
Cinnamon Path Productions is hosting a reading of a new data center farce by one of our favorite writers. We’ve assembled a fantastic Austin cast—including Kelsey Mazak, Pablo Muñoz-Evers, Will Douglas, and David DuBose—and we’d love your feedback as we work through this play-in-development.

20261117-the-mousetrap-by-theatre-victor.venue_name: Leo J. Welder Center for the Performing Arts
20261117-the-mousetrap-by-theatre-victor.html_synopsis: The Mousetrap opened in the West End of London in 1952, and has been running continuously since with over 25,000 performances. It is the longest running show (of any type) of the modern era. Written by the famous Agatha Christie, this murder mystery will have you guessing throughout and is known for its twist ending, which the audiences are traditionally asked not to reveal after leaving the theatre.

20261105-bisexual-sadness-by-jarrott-pro.title: Bisexual Sadness by Jarrott Productions
20261105-bisexual-sadness-by-jarrott-pro.venue_address: Black Box Theatre, 4th floor, First Baptist Church 901 Trinity Street Austin, TX, 78701
20261105-bisexual-sadness-by-jarrott-pro.rss_description_html:
Faye is getting married to a man she truly loves, but at the same time wishing he was a woman. She’s sad that she will have to fight harder to be a part of the queer communities in which she’s always found a home.

Bisexual Sadness is about what it sounds like—the specific loneliness of being a bisexual woman in love with a straight man. It treats with curiosity and respect the questions of belonging, identity, cultural migrations and kinship.

And did we mention it’s a comedy?

 

Jarrott Productions Producing Artistic Director Will Gibson Douglas, whom you’ve seen on stage in our productions of Signficant Other, The Lifespan of a Fact, and The Shark is Broken, and who directed Home, I’m Darling and A Million More To Go, will direct this production, in its Southwest Regional Premiere.

 

From Will Gibson Douglas:

 

The title is a joke. It’s also completely true. That tension is the point.

 

Bisexual people are now the largest part of the LGBTQ+ community — and, according to recent research, they also report feeling the least connected to it.

 

We have our own specific issues, and our own specific privileges. India’s play brilliantly explores that complex specificity. It is messy. This “sadness” is one I know myself, and one I’ve seen in friends of mine, navigating relationships and marriages that will appear “straight” to everyone. How do you fit into a community you feel a part of, but no longer seem to fit into? Do you have to live in that “sadness” forever?

 

I don’t have a tidy answer. I don’t know if there is one. What I do have is a belief that the specificity of stories is what allows us to find truth in ourselves. You don’t have to be bisexual to know what it’s like to belong to more than one world at once, and to watch people insist you pick a side.

 

And somehow, the play is funny. Genuinely, in a real-life way. It also packs an absolute punch. It is messy.

 

I didn’t get to grow up seeing myself in stories. I am allowed to see myself in this one. I invite you to see yourself in it as well.

 

I’m grateful to India for trusting us with only the second production of this play ever, and immensely proud that Jarrott Productions gets to be the room where this story gets told specifically — a story that is not a stand-in for queerness generally, but as itself. I think you’re going to love it. I think it’s going to challenge you. And I look forward to both.

 

It is messy.

 

Will Gibson Douglas

20270406-macbeth-by-san-pedro-playhouse.rss_description_html:
Ambition fueled by love and prophecy drives a Scottish nobleman to seize the crown at any cost. But in Shakespeare’s darkest tragedy, Macbeth and Lady Macbeth discover that the things we do for power can corrupt even the strongest bonds of love. Experience this timeless tale under the stars in historic San Pedro Springs Park for our beloved Shakespeare in the Park tradition. Now in our fourth year of producing outdoor Shakespeare, this cherished tradition continues to bring bold, accessible storytelling to the heart of the community. Join us for an unforgettable evening of drama, atmosphere, and one of the Bard’s most gripping tales.
 
Featuring Anthony and Asia Ciaravino.

Recommended for ages 13 and up.

20261203-its-a-wonderful-life-a-live-rad.title: It's A Wonderful Life, a Live Radio Play by Classic Theatre of San Antonio
20261203-its-a-wonderful-life-a-live-rad.venue_name: Cellar Theatre, San Pedro Playhouse, San Antonio
20261203-its-a-wonderful-life-a-live-rad.venue_address: San Pedro Park 800 W Ashby Place San Antonio, TX, 78212
20261203-its-a-wonderful-life-a-live-rad.rss_description_html:
Step into a 1940s radio studio for this heartwarming holiday classic! When George Bailey hits rock bottom on Christmas Eve, an angel shows him just how much one life can matter. A joyful reminder that love, sacrifice, and community create ripples far beyond what we can see.
 
Inspired by Frank Capra's timeless film It’s a Wonderful Life, this theatrical retelling captures the magic of live storytelling while echoing one of its most cherished sentiments: “Every time a bell rings, an angel gets his wings.”
 
Filled with nostalgia, warmth, and a touch of holiday wonder, this beloved story invites audiences to rediscover the power of hope and the extraordinary impact of an ordinary life.

Recommended for ages 8 and up

20270128-the-mountaintop-by-classic-thea.title: The Mountaintop by Classic Theatre of San Antonio
20270128-the-mountaintop-by-classic-thea.venue_name: Cellar Theatre, San Pedro Playhouse, San Antonio
20270128-the-mountaintop-by-classic-thea.venue_address: San Pedro Park 800 W Ashby Place San Antonio, TX, 78212
20270128-the-mountaintop-by-classic-thea.rss_description_html:
On the eve of his assassination, Dr. Martin Luther King Jr. spends his final night in Room 306 of the Lorraine Motel. In Katori Hall’s intimate reimagining, we witness a man wrestling with his legacy, his fears, and his unwavering love for justice and his people.
 
Winner of the Olivier Award for Best New Play, this powerful drama blends realism with poetic imagination, revealing the humanity behind the icon. With striking theatricality and emotional depth, The Mountaintop invites audiences to reflect on the weight of a dream—and the enduring impact of a life devoted to change.

20270219-a-chorus-line-by-san-pedro-play.title: A Chorus Line by San Pedro Playhouse
20270219-a-chorus-line-by-san-pedro-play.venue_name: Russell Hill Rogers Stage, San Pedro Playhouse, San Antonio
20270219-a-chorus-line-by-san-pedro-play.venue_address: 800 West Ashby Place San Antonio, TX, 78212
20270219-a-chorus-line-by-san-pedro-play.rss_description_html:
Seventeen dancers. One job. Everything they’ve got. In a bare Broadway rehearsal studio, these performers lay it all on the line, sharing the sacrifices, heartbreaks, and dreams that brought them here. Because when you love what you do this much, you risk everything to be one singular sensation.
 
Winner of nine Tony Awards and one of Broadway’s longest-running musicals, A Chorus Line captures the grit, glamour, and heart of life on the stage.
 
 Bursting with iconic numbers like “One,” “I Hope I Get It,” and “What I Did for Love,” this groundbreaking musical remains a powerful celebration of ambition, artistry, and the courage it takes to chase your dreams.
 
Directed by RIck Sanchez,Pedro Playhouse's Vice President of Artistic Programming.
 
Choreographer Dena Mabry, Music Director Andrew Hendley!

20260918-how-to-succeed-in-business-with.title: How to Succeed in Business Without Really Trying by The Theatre Company (TTC)
20260918-how-to-succeed-in-business-with.venue_address: 3125 S. Texas Ave., Suite 500 (behind Joann Fabrics in the Tejas Center) Bryan, TX, 77802
20260918-how-to-succeed-in-business-with.rss_description_html: How to Succeed in Business Without Really Trying, the Pulitzer-Prize-and-Tony-Award-winning musical, is a story about the triumph of the common man amid the buffoonery of big business. When a restless, creative, and ambitious window washer named J. Pierrepont Finch happens upon a book entitled 'How to Succeed in Business Without Really Trying', he decides to begin his rise up the corporate ladder. With the book’s instructions and a dose of his own cleverness, Finch starts by landing a job in the mailroom at the World Wide Wicket Company. He is soon promoted and outsmarts his scheming, sniveling rival, Frump - who also happens to be the boss's nephew-- before finally reaching the very top of the organization.

20260828-avenue-q-by-city-theatre-compan.title: Avenue Q by City Theatre Company
20260828-avenue-q-by-city-theatre-compan.venue_address: Genesis Creative Collective 1507 Wilshire Blvd Austin, TX, 78722
20260828-avenue-q-by-city-theatre-compan.rss_description_html:
Avenue Q. Where do you live when the only address you can afford when fresh out of college, out of a job, or just trying to find your way in life? You live on Avenue Q! Part flesh, part felt, and packed with heart, this unforgettable bunch of puppets - and their neighborhood friends - discover that life’s biggest lessons aren’t always as simple as they seem. Princeton, Kate Monster, Gary Coleman (yes, that one!), Christmas Eve, Rod, Nicky, and their newfound friends (played by talented actors and puppets) valiantly seek jobs, dates, and their ever-elusive purpose in life. The laugh-out-loud musical show - with furries and friends – just trying to find their way in this crazy, crazy world. Sharp wit, catchy songs, a wicked sense of humor, and winner of the Tony Award “Triple Crown.” Don't miss out on this musical hit!
 
The Tony-Award-winning musical that is part flesh, part felt, and packed with so much heart!
 
Music and Lyrics by Jeff Marx and Robert Lopez. Book by Jeff Whitty

20270513-summer-1976-by-jarrott-producti.title: Summer, 1976 by Jarrott Productions
20270513-summer-1976-by-jarrott-producti.rss_description_html:
David Auburn’s play takes place against the backdrop of Viet Nam and the Watergate years that. Summer, 1976 follows two women living in Ohio who become unlikely friends over playdates with their young daughters during the summer of 1976, the American Bicentennial.

New York Times called Summer, 1976 a “bittersweet, comic memory play — a story of profound connection,” while the Wall Street Journal called it “warm and beguiling,” and Deadline said it “captures an experience that’s as universal as it is inexplicable: a friendship that shouldn’t work, but does.”

Director Jarrott Reflects on the Summer of 1976

I was still in radio that summer, playing hot hits on KNOW like Johnnie Taylor’s Disco Lady, Paul McCartney’s Silly Love Songs, and Elton John and Kiki Dee’s summer smash Don’t Go Breaking My Heart.

I was supposed to emcee the Austin Symphony concert (with fireworks) on Auditorium Shores on July 4th, but the event got rained out. Just as well, in a way, as my current wife at the time (#2, but who’s counting) was sick with the flu.

I was still in radio that summer, playing hot hits on KNOW like Johnnie Taylor’s Disco Lady, Paul McCartney’s Silly Love Songs, and Elton John and Kiki Dee’s summer smash Don’t Go Breaking My Heart.

I was supposed to emcee the Austin Symphony concert (with fireworks) on Auditorium Shores on July 4th, but the event got rained out. Just as well, in a way, as my current wife at the time (#2, but who’s counting) was sick with the flu.

At Austin movie theatres, The Omen, Midway, and Logan’s Run were big hits; while nationwide, Operation Sail and the Freedom Train were iconic events celebrating the 200th anniversary of the adoption of the Declaration of Independence.

These and other widespread community events and festivals helped lift the national mood as we came out of the Viet Nam and Watergate years.

I was fortunate to see the original Broadway production in April 2023 and I walked out of the theatre knowing that I wanted to bring this play to Austin audiences. We’ve been trying to get the rights to produce this play for the past two years, and were just recently successful.

I’m so grateful to be able to bring you this work that’s been living in my brain and my heart for the past three years. And even more grateful to announce the amazing cast of two!

 

 

I’ve known Johanna Whitmore for ages, and admired her artistry as an actor as well as a director and much-loved educator. We are forever grateful that she sent us Tucker Shepherd (Admissions, The Sound Inside) and Kaitlyn Hartnagel (our props guru). For some reason our professional lives have never aligned and I’ve never had the privilege of working with her — until now. Johanna will star as Alice.

Appearing opposite Johanna as Diane is a new star in the Austin theatre constellation, Mimi Strum. You saw her as FLOTUS in 2024’s smash hit POTUS. New to Austin at the time, Mimi auditioned for JP for that role, I was gobsmacked. I’ve been searching for a role for her since then and I think she is the perfect choice to bring Diane to life.

20270320-pinocchio-davies-by-magik-theat.title: Pinocchio (Davies) by Magik Theatre
20270320-pinocchio-davies-by-magik-theat.rss_description_html:
One of the most beloved characters in children’s literature takes center stage in this magical re-telling, which blends opera and theatrical staging. Pinocchio captures the childlike curiosity in all of us as he navigates an unknown and complicated world. When persuaded by the mischievous duo, Wolf and Cat, Pinocchio disobeys his father, Gepetto, and skips school. Of course, his journey is met by the notorious Dr. Dulcamara, a loathsome puppeteer, and his mechanical doll Olympia. Through a series of adventures, Pinocchio learns the harsh reality that every untruth comes with real-world consequences, the importance of sharing the truth with trusted grownups, and ultimately, the meaning of family. Your favorite wooden marionette comes alive for 3-weekends only in this age-old story of truthfulness, bravery, and heart! San Antonio’s not-to-miss artistic collaboration of 2027.

By John Davies
Based on The Adventures of Pinocchio by Carlo Collodi with scenes from operas by Mozart, Donizetti, Offenbach, and Pergolesi

Magik Theatre & OPERA San Antonio present John Davies’ Pinocchio, a one-act opera for young audiences based on Carlo Collodi’s literary classic, featuring music from operas by Mozart, Donizetti, Offenbach, and Pergolesi.


Recommended for ages 4+
Running Time: 55 minutes
Language: English

"Every dog has its day. Every marriage has its limits."
 
In this fetchingly romantic comedy, Greg brings home a street-smart, hilarious stray named Sylvia, upending his life and putting his marriage to the ultimate test. It offers a wonderful look into the complexities of love and commitment, begging the question: How do you choose between the love of your life and man’s best friend?
 
 
Don't miss this heartwarming comedy about love, loyalty, and learning to share the couch.
 
PG (13) Adult Themes & Language

20270219-the-best-of-the-carol-burnett-s.rss_description_html:
Carol Burnett is known as one of the most brilliant comedians of all time, and her CAROL BURNETT SHOW ran for 11 years, garnering 25 prime-time Emmy awards and inclusion on Time magazine’s list of “100 Best TV Shows of All Times.”  This event features the actual scripts to some of her best comedy sketches, as they were performed by the unsurpassed comedy team of Burnett, Harvey Korman, Tim Conway, and Vickie Lawrence.  Not a word in these scripts has been changed, bringing the brilliance of the sketches to a new generation of performers and audience members.  
 
Following the tremendous success of this event in the spring of 2026, we’re bringing it back— with new sketches and a new location at the historic Texas Theater!  Featuring a blend of community members and the students of TheatreXpress, this showcase promises to be a blend of nostalgia and laugh-out-loud fun for all!

20261030-dracula-a-comedy-of-terrors-by-.title: Dracula - A Comedy of Terrors by Texas Lutheran University Dramatic Media
20261030-dracula-a-comedy-of-terrors-by-.rss_description_html:
When her sister Mina falls ill with a mysterious disease of the blood, Lucy Westfeldt and her fiancé, Jonathan Harker, enlist the help of famed vampire hunter Doctor Jean Van Helsing. Their hunt for the dangerous and sexy Count Dracula abounds with madcap antics, clever wordplay, and gags galore.  Perfect for the Halloween season, join us for this brilliantly comic take on the classic tale that is guaranteed to induce blood-curdling screams— of laughter!
 
You’ve never seen a DRACULA this funny!  It’s as if the legendary vampire feasted on the blood of Mel Brooks, the team from Monty Python, and your favorite glam rocker.  The result is a lightning-fast, laugh-out-loud, 90-minute, gender-bending romp!

20260821-35mm-a-musical-exhibition-by-th.title: 35mm: A Musical Exhibition by The Theatre Company (TTC)
20260821-35mm-a-musical-exhibition-by-th.venue_address: 3125 S. Texas Ave., Suite 500 (behind Joann Fabrics in the Tejas Center) Bryan, TX, 77802
20260821-35mm-a-musical-exhibition-by-th.rss_description_html:
The Theatre Company of Bryan - College Station (TTC) presents 35mm: A MUSICAL EXHIBITION, the first “Off the Menu” (OTM) production of Season 37, Because of Randy. Like other OTM shows, 35MM provides local audiences with the rare opportunity to experience live musical theatre performances of less widely recognized yet critically acclaimed and culturally significant musical theatre. TTC is proud to bring these productions to life in our community.

Featuring music and lyrics by the award-winning Ryan Scott Oliver and inspired by the internationally recognized photography of Matthew Murphy, this multimedia musical experience is based on “snapshot stories,” each woven into a song and a specific photographic moment. Each photo creates a song to produce a moment in time, a split second of a life unfolding. 35MM explores life’s important themes— love, death, memory, friendship, betrayal—presented in what many have hailed as a groundbreaking example of what modern American musicals can be.

The show opened Off-Broadway in 2012 and has played in theaters all over the world since then. An original cast album was also released in 2012. Reviewers praised its fusion of mediums and its innovative vision of multimedia theatre, as well as its depth and ability to move audiences deeply. Featuring an all-star cast of TTC voices and directed by Savannah Barrera and Keri Kempf, 35mm is not to be missed!

20260904-cinderella-the-musical-by-rodge.title: Cinderella, the musical by Rodgers and Hammerstein by Angelo Civic Theatre
20260904-cinderella-the-musical-by-rodge.rss_description_html: The timeless enchantment of a magical fairy tale is reborn with the Rodgers & Hammerstein hallmarks of originality, charm and elegance. Originally presented on television in 1957 starring Julie Andrews, Rodgers & Hammerstein's Cinderella was the most widely viewed program in the history of the medium. Its recreation in 1965 starring Lesley Ann Warren was no less successful in transporting a new generation to the miraculous kingdom of dreams-come-true, and so was a second remake in 1997, which starred Brandy as Cinderella and Whitney Houston as her Fairy Godmother.

The exhibition celebrates the legendary designer who created the costumes for Walt Disney's original Mary Poppins film, bringing colorful flair to Edwardian England on screen.

20261204-a-christmas-carol-davis-and-bea.title: A Christmas Carol (Davis and Beaver) by The Archive Theater Company
20261204-a-christmas-carol-davis-and-bea.rss_description_html:
A Christmas Carol is a direct stage adaptation of Charles Dicken's 1843 novella. Adapted for the stage by Jennifer Rose Davis and Lynn Schaeffer Beaver, the play takes us through the classic story on one man's redemption and reclamation from a life of selfishness and greed through the intervention of the spirit world. It contains themes of personal redemption, social justice, human connection, and family love.

Directed by Elizabeth V. Newman.

This is a joint production between The Archive Theater, The Filigree Theatre, and Pioneer Farms.

20260927-at-the-edge-of-nowhere-by-filig.title: At the Edge of Nowhere by Filigree Theatre
20260927-at-the-edge-of-nowhere-by-filig.rss_description_html:
What happens when a seventeen-year-old girl discovers she is pregnant in the weeks following the overturning of Roe v. Wade?

Set in a small rural Texas town, At the Edge of Nowhere follows Sadie as she carries a secret that could mean her future is no longer her own. As she navigates family expectations, town gossip, religious judgment, and political division, the voices around her become a chorus of fear and pressure that threatens to drown out her own thoughts.
 
 

Wallace Too Productions and The Filigree Theatre will present the staged reading of At the Edge of Nowhere, Sabrina Wallace's debut one-act stage play.

Directed by Elizabeth V. Newman, the reading is presented as part of The Filigree Theatre's Stage One Reading Series, a workshop series dedicated to the development of new works by established and emerging playwrights and screenwriters.

 
"At the Edge of Nowhere was born from a conversation with my daughter, Emma, who was twenty when the Dobbs decision was handed down,” said playwright Sabrina Wallace. “We started with a terrifying question that quickly opened up many more: What goes through the mind of a young woman who discovers she is pregnant? Does she want to be a mother? Does she want to be pregnant? What options does she have, and how much time does she have to decide? Sadie’s story grew from those questions and from exploring women’s choices in post-Roe Texas, where restrictive laws, religion, politics, and fear can make it harder for a young woman to make a decision that is truly her own.”

 

The reading will be directed by Elizabeth V. Newman, Producing Artistic Director of The Filigree Theatre, the award-winning, critically-acclaimed theatre company. A native New Yorker, based in Austin, TX, Newman’s theatre productions have been awarded multiple Austin Theatre Critics awards (including Outstanding Director of Three Plays) and numerous nominations (including Outstanding Production) and B. Iden Payne awards and nominations (including Outstanding Direction of a Drama, Outstanding Production of a Drama). She has received multiple awards for her short films, feature film and short & feature screenplays including “Best Female Director”(Pizza My Heart), “Best Director Independent Feature Film”& “Best Director Feature Film” (Child of Light) “Best Feature Screenplay” (Shattering…) She is a member of DIRECTOR’S LAB: NORTH (Toronto) and served as the Founding Co-President of Women in Film and Television: Austin (WIFT-AUSTIN). She has twice served as a panelist at The Austin Film Festival. She graduated with honors from Yale University with dual B.A. degrees in History of Art and Theater Studies. She earned her M.F.A. in Film Production at Boston University. For more information, please see: ElizabethVNewman.com and FiligreeTheatre.com 

 

About the Playwright

Sabrina Wallace is an Argentine-American playwright, producer, and theatre advocate based in Austin, Texas. At the Edge of Nowhere is her debut stage play and the first in a developing series of works centred on women's experiences. Through intimate, character-driven storytelling, Wallace explores themes of family, reproductive rights, marriage, divorce, immigration, and the moments that quietly reshape ordinary lives. www.linktr.ee/SabrinaWallace

 

About Wallace Too Productions

Wallace Too Productions is an independent production company dedicated to developing and supporting bold, thought-provoking theatre. Producing credits include Dear England (UK, Olivier Award for Best New Play), The Prom (US, Drama Desk Award for Outstanding Musical), 13 Going on 30: The Musical (UK), and Freaky Friday (UK). Investment credits include The Outsiders (Tony Award for Best Musical), Sunset Blvd. (Tony Award for Best Revival of a Musical), The Inheritance (Tony Award for Best Play), and Company (Tony Award for Best Revival of a Musical). www.wallacetoo.co.uk

 

About The Filigree Theatre

"To filigree” means "to make by hand and with much skill.” The Filigree Theatre is an award-winning, critically-acclaimed independent theatre company committed to producing high-level, professional theatre by creating thoughtful and innovative work for the stage, ranging from classic plays to new works and world premieres. The company embraces the dual roots of the word ‘Filigree’ (filum 'thread' and granum ‘seed’) in its mission, with an aim to serve both as a seed by originating work in Filigree’s home-base of Austin, TX, and as a thread by collaborating with artists and engaging audiences in other theatre hubs such as New York & Los Angeles. Artistic Director, Elizabeth V. Newman https://www.filigreetheatre.com/

 

About The Filigree Theatre’s Stage One Reading Series 

Stage One is The Filigree Theatre's staged reading workshop series, presented in partnership with EVN Productions, that supports the development of new plays and screenplays by established and emerging writers while connecting playwrights, directors, actors, and audiences through the creative process.

Through intimate, character-driven storytelling, Wallace explores themes of family, reproductive rights, marriage, divorce, immigration, and the moments that quietly reshape ordinary lives. www.linktr.ee/SabrinaWallace About Wallace Too Productions Wallace Too Productions is an independent production company dedicated to developing and supporting bold, thought-provoking theatre. Producing credits include Dear England (UK, Olivier Award for Best New Play), The Prom (US, Drama Desk Award for Outstanding Musical), 13 Going on 30: The Musical (UK), and Freaky Friday (UK). Investment credits include The Outsiders (Tony Award for Best Musical), Sunset Blvd. (Tony Award for Best Revival of a Musical), The Inheritance (Tony Award for Best Play), and Company (Tony Award for Best Revival of a Musical). www.wallacetoo.co.uk About The Filigree Theatre "To filigree” means "to make by hand and with much skill.” The Filigree Theatre is an award-winning, critically-acclaimed independent theatre company committed to producing high-level, professional theatre by creating thoughtful and innovative work for the stage, ranging from classic plays to new works and world premieres. The company embraces the dual roots of the word ‘Filigree’ (filum 'thread' and granum ‘seed’) in its mission, with an aim to serve both as a seed by originating work in Filigree’s home-base of Austin, TX, and as a thread by collaborating with artists and engaging audiences in other theatre hubs such as New York & Los Angeles. Artistic Director, Elizabeth V. Newman https://www.filigreetheatre.com/ About The Filigree Theatre’s Stage One Reading Series Stage One is The Filigree Theatre's staged reading workshop series, presented in partnership with EVN Productions, that supports the development of new plays and screenplays by established and emerging writers while connecting playwrights, directors, actors, and audiences through the creative process.

20270422-macbeth-by-mclennan-community-c.title: Macbeth by McLennan Community College
20270422-macbeth-by-mclennan-community-c.rss_description_html:
“Fair is foul, and foul is fair.”

Through the glens and over the highlands of medieval Scotland, war rages between clans and chieftains vying for power and territory. Brave Macbeth has fought valiantly on the battlefield for his liege, Duncan, King of Scotland. Titles and riches are his by might and right, but are they enough? A chance meeting with three “weird sisters” reveals he is owed much more, perhaps even the very throne. Perhaps, but at what cost? In a world where crowns and kingdoms are forged in blood and steel, Shakespeare weaves a psychological, supernatural thriller for the ages.

20270226-fiddler-on-the-roof-by-mclennan.title: Fiddler on the Roof by McLennan Community College
20270226-fiddler-on-the-roof-by-mclennan.rss_description_html:
One of the most beloved and storied musicals of all time bounds onto the boards of the Ball Performing Arts Center in a joint adventure between McLennan Opera and Theatre. In Czarist Russia, we find Tevye, a humble milkman, and his wife, Golde, making their way as they raise five daughters in their small Jewish village of Anatevka. In 1905, not even Tevye’s hamlet is immune to the ever-encroaching modern world and the growing specter of antisemitism. While grasping onto his traditions and dreams, Tevye hopes to forge a prosperous future life for his daughters, but they, and the changing world, may have other ideas. Winner of nine Tony Awards and three Oscars, Fiddler on the Roof features an amazing score with enduring classics like “If I Were a Rich Man,” “Matchmaker, Matchmaker,” and “Sunrise, Sunset” that will lift your spirits and warm your heart.

Book by Joseph Stein; Music by Jerry Bock; Lyrics by Sheldon Harnick

Original Production Directed & Choreographed by Jerome Robbins

Based on Sholem Aleichem's stories, by special permission of Arnold Perl

20270421-mean-girls-by-baylor-university.title: Mean Girls by Baylor University Theatre
20270421-mean-girls-by-baylor-university.venue_name: Jones Auditorium, Hooper-Schaefer Fine Arts Center
20270421-mean-girls-by-baylor-university.rss_description_html:
Tina Fey’s hit film Mean Girls comes to life in this hilarious, high-energy musical about the perils of popularity and the power of staying true to yourself. 


High school is a jungle, and no one knows that better than Cady Heron. After moving to North Shore High, she quickly learns that the fiercest predators wear pink on Wednesdays.  


Welcomed into the world of the Plastics, she discovers that the quest for popularity can come at the cost of friendship, kindness, and knowing who you really are. With infectious music, sharp humor, and unforgettable characters, Mean Girls proves that the most powerful thing you can be is yourself. 

Content Advisory: This production contains strong language, mature humor, depictions of bullying, references to body image and eating disorders, alcohol use, and suggestive content. Recommended for teen and adult audiences.

Written by Tina Fey, lyrics by Nell Benjamin, and music by Jeff Richmond
Directed by Lauren Mikeal Weber

20261110-big-love-by-baylor-university-t.title: Big Love by Baylor University Theatre
20261110-big-love-by-baylor-university-t.rss_description_html:
Love is messy, and that’s been true since the times of ancient Greece. In Charles Mee’s timeless adaptation of Aeschylus’ The Suppliants, fifty sisters flee to a foreign land to escape forced marriages to their fifty cousins. Plates shatter, sparks fly, and blood is shed at this violent collision point between men and women, familiar and foreign, and poetic and political.  

Content Advisory: foul language, depictions of violence, sexual violence, sex, homosexuality, and blood.

Written by Charles Mee
Directed by Natalie Guess
In partial fulfillment of the MFA in Directing

20261119-silent-sky-by-mclennan-communit.title: Silent Sky by McLennan Community College
20261119-silent-sky-by-mclennan-communit.rss_description_html: It is the early 1900s. The field of astronomy is dominated by gifted but provincial men; however, the rigidity of this exclusive atmosphere does not assuage the young and brilliant Henrietta Leavitt from reaching for the stars. Working at the Harvard Observatory, Henrietta is one of several women tasked with assessing and cataloging star charts for an esteemed astronomer. Discontent with performing calculations like a simple computer while “greater” men take credit for her discoveries, Henrietta pushes back against social norms despite the ramifications for her familial and romantic relationships. In Silent Sky, playwright Lauren Gunderson deftly crafts the vivid, true story of Henrietta Leavitt’s personal struggle to break through the glass ceiling while searching for truth and innovation in the heavens.

20261001-erma-bombeck-at-wits-end-by-aus.title: Erma Bombeck: At Wit's End by Austin Playhouse
20261001-erma-bombeck-at-wits-end-by-aus.rss_description_html:
Erma Bombeck: At Wit’s End is a one-woman play that humorously explores the life of the beloved columnist Erma Bombeck, highlighting her experiences as a suburban housewife and her advocacy for women's rights. The play captures her wit and the everyday struggles faced by women, making it both entertaining and relatable.

Born Erma Fiste, Erma Louise Bombeck, achieved great popularity for a newspaper column that comically depicted suburban home life in the second half of the 20th century. With a career spanning decades, Bombeck published 4,000 newspaper articles from the 60s to the 90s. During the 70s, her witty columns were read, twice weekly, by thirty million readers of 900 newspapers in the US and Canada with the majority of her 15 books becoming instant best sellers.

Starring Sarah Fleming Walker as Erma Bombeck.

Directed by Lara Toner Haddock.

Age Recommendation: Recommended for ages 13 and up for minimal mentions of adult situations; Children under 5 are not permitted.

20260903-gruesome-playground-injuries-by.rss_description_html:
Over the course of 30 years, the lives of Kayleen and Doug intersect at the most bizarre intervals, leading the two childhood friends to compare scars and the physical calamities that keep drawing them together. The two friends and would-be lovers meet at eight years old in the nurse’s office of their elementary school; Kayleen has a painful stomach ache and Doug a nasty scrape.
 
As they grow up, they continue to come back to each other, brought together by injury, heartbreak and their own self-destructive tendencies. This compelling and intimate love story is sure to captivate audiences.
 
Featuring SATX artists: Lauren Campion, Ivan Ortega, Gabriella Ramirez, & Kevin Engel.
 
Directed by Lili Sanchez, asst. Sara Cantu.

20261101-the-american-revolution-by-the-.title: The American Revolution by The Zahir
20261101-the-american-revolution-by-the-.rss_description_html:
Join this hilarious and historical patriotic parade that follows General George Washington on his quest to defeat the British Empire and secure independence. Along the way, he confronts Redcoats, Tories, Hessian mercenaries, mutinying generals, a bankrupt Congress, spies, and Benedict Arnold. He is joined by the world's most incompetent and endearing troop of new recruits: The Rebel Mess. These rambunctious Yankees tumble through the colonies chasing freedom, dodging bullets, making song, and discovering what it means to be an American.

About the Playwright

Kirk Wood Bromley, aka “Shakespeare on mushrooms” (LA Weekly) and “the beloved bard of downtown theater” (The New Yorker), has been writing verse plays since 1990, and in that time his work has been produced by Aaron Beall (Nada, NYC), Ben Yalom (FoolsFury, SF), Bad Epitaph (Cleveland), Sacred Fools (LA), Wesleyan, Kenyon, Mizzou, Inverse Theater (of which he is Artistic Director), and more. Bromley and/or Inverse have won numerous awards, including Best Downtown Theater Company (NY Press 2001), the Berrilla Kerr Foundation Playwriting Award (2001), three NY Fringe Festival Excellence Awards (2002, 2003, 2009), and the first Caffe Cino Award (NY Innovative Theatre Awards 2005). While he has been compared to Shakespeare (NY Magazine, Time Out NY, OffOffOff.com, the Cleveland Scene), Stoppard (The Village Voice), and Van Gogh (NYTheatre.com), his writing “speaks directly to its audience's concerns and in its dialect” (American Theatre Magazine). More about him, his theater company, and his band (The Good Hard) can be found at kirkwoodbromley.com.

About the French Legation

One of the oldest houses in Austin, the French Legation opened in 1841 as a home and diplomatic outpost for the French chargé d'affaires to the Republic of Texas, Alphonse Dubois, after France recognized the Republic of Texas as a sovereign nation. The site tells the story of Texas' settlement and the growth of one of the capital city's most vibrant neighborhoods.

About The Zahir

Led by artistic director and award-winning playwright L.B. Deyo, The Zahir's mission is to create obsession-worthy theater that draws people out of isolation and back into conversation. Learn more at the-zahir.org.

These rambunctious Yankees tumble through the colonies chasing freedom, dodging bullets, making song, and discovering what it means to be an American.

20260904-the-barbie-dream-heist-by-the-s.title: Barbie Dream Heist by The Spark
20260904-the-barbie-dream-heist-by-the-s.venue_address: inside at 2307 Manor Road Austin, TX, 78722
20260904-the-barbie-dream-heist-by-the-s.rss_description_html:
Follow five Barbies and one Ken as they band together to stop Clos.IT in a scheme threatening to sabotage their spring fashion show. Inspired by the animated series Life in the Dreamhouse that many Spark ensemble members grew up watching, the show uses comedy and physical storytelling to take on very real issues — the encroachment of AI on creative work, and its environmental cost — without ever losing its sense of fun.

"This is a show about friendship holding the line against forces trying to replace what people make with their hands and hearts," said Sharky Meehan, director and performer. "It just happens to be told through six plastic dolls fighting for their fashion show."

The Spark, La Fenice's youth production arm, presents its first fully devised original work — written, directed, designed, and performed entirely by local teens. Barbie Dream Heist, an hour-long original physical comedy, marks The Spark's second show and its first fully devised piece, created start to finish by Austin-area teenagers — the majority of whom identify as LGBTQIA+.

The Spark's members have spent two years training in corporeal mime, Commedia dell'Arte and mask work alongside La Fenice's adult company members. Barbie Dream Heist is the first time that training has been put entirely in young artists' own hands: from script and direction to performance and design, every creative decision in the show belongs to its teenage company.

The Barbie Dream Heist, presented by The Spark (La Fenice's youth production arm).

The Spark is La Fenice's youth production arm, training Austin-area teens in arts administration and physical theatre performance alongside La Fenice's professional company members. Barbie Dream Heist is The Spark's second production and its first fully devised original work.

La Fenice is an Austin-based physical theatre company specializing in Commedia dell'Arte and immersive, devised performance.

20261029-welcome-to-terror-terrace-by-fa.title: Welcome to Terror Terrace by Fallout Theatre
20261029-welcome-to-terror-terrace-by-fa.rss_description_html:
Welcome to Terror Terrace is a Halloween-themed musical comedy variety show (with a sexy, throwback flair). The loose narrative throughline follows a group of monster tenants after they learn their landlord plans to sell their decrepit apartment building.

Thanks to funding from the City of Austin Elevate grant, this show is our most ambitious production to date. This show features original songs and sketches, burlesque, drag, professional dancers, and a full cast of our favorite weirdos in the city. We’ve been working on it since the beginning of the year and we’re so excited to share it with Austin!
