20261015-sullivan-and-gilbert-by-gilbert.title: Sullivan and Gilbert by Gilbert & Sullivan Austin
20261015-sullivan-and-gilbert-by-gilbert.rss_description_html:
Rehearsals gone wrong! Queen Victoria wants a revue and calls on her favorite music makers Sullivan and Gilbert. But—Sullivan’s in love but won’t say with whom; and the Queen’s cheerfully bumbling son Alfred is flirting with the ladies (and wants to join the cast). Not to mention that Sullivan and Gilbert have been feuding for years. The songs are familiar but dances are new -- and it's almost showtime!

 

Part docudrama, part period comedy, and definitely "Gilbert and Sullivan's Greatest Hits," this delightful revue from Ken Ludwig, author of Lend Me a Tenor, Leading Ladies, Murder on the Orient Express and Moon Over Buffalo is sure to amuse!

 

Entertaining and educating Texas audiences since 1976, Gilbert & Sullivan Austin is dedicated to spreading the topsy-turvy humor and joyful music of W. S. Gilbert and Arthur Sullivan. The company will stage its summer grand production in June (in 2027, The Pirates of Penzance) and various musicales and events during the season. To celebrate its 50th year of performances featuring casts, musicians, and technical crews exclusively from the greater Austin area, the company is collaborating with Austin Playhouse to stage a five-performance run of Ken Ludwig's early success Sullivan and Gilbert (1983, presented at the Kennedy Center in 1988).

20261113-if-these-walls-could-talk-by-k-.title: If These Walls Could Talk by K Zamore
20261113-if-these-walls-could-talk-by-k-.rss_description_html:
If These Walls Could Talk is a deeply moving, hilarious, and soul-stirring stage play written and directed by Dr. Kerry Ann Zamore Byrd that explores the sacred bond of sisterhood through an unforgettable blend of gripping drama, uplifting gospel music, and laugh-out-loud comedy. Set around a dining room table as five diverse Black women ranging from ages 25 to 65 gather to prepare a meal, a simple spill on the wall opens the floodgates to their most guarded truths—unpacking raw, relatable stories of infidelity, devastating divorce, the unfiltered realities of menopause, domestic violence, and the grief of widowhood.

More than just a night of theater, this powerful production serves as a spiritual experience and a triumphant celebration of faith, resilience, and healing, reminding every audience member that no matter how heavy life’s burdens may get, you never have to carry them alone

20261106-the-curious-savage-by-city-thea.title: The Curious Savage by City Theatre Company
20261106-the-curious-savage-by-city-thea.venue_address: Genesis Creative Collective 1507 Wilshire Blvd Austin, TX, 78722
20261106-the-curious-savage-by-city-thea.rss_description: When Ethel Savage’s late husband leaves her a small fortune, she creates a fund to support dreamers with whimsical ambitions. But her three greedy stepchildren—a socialite, a senator, and a judge—commit her to a mental institution, hoping to “bring her to her senses.” At the sanitarium, a warm and welcoming place called The Cloisters, Ethel befriends the other “guests,” a colorful group of kind, generous, and delusional souls, while her stepchildren search for her fortune. With warmth, humor, and dignity, John Patrick’s masterful comedy celebrates those often overlooked and reminds us of the power of kindness, affection, and empathy in a world that too often rewards greed and ambition. Directed by Payton Trahan.

20260926-romeo-katrina-by-color-arc-prod.title: Romeo & Katrina by Color Arc Productions
20260926-romeo-katrina-by-color-arc-prod.rss_description_html:
Set four years post-Hurricane Katrina, our story crosses the Mississippi River to bridge two lovers from Westbank and Eastbank New Orleans: Romeo Tran and Katrina "Trina" Batiste. Romeo and Trina's relationship grows amidst the backdrop of New Orleans’ post-Katrina recovery and the Saints’ storied ascent to Superbowl glory.
Performed by an all-Vietnamese American and Black cast of Austin actors, ROMEO AND KATRINA is an uplifting exploration of community, life, and finding light in dark places. It is inspired by Shakespeare's Romeo and Juliet and Hamlet.
 
A live script reading.
